newsitem.title: USA: Firm settles with CFTC, SEC over derivatives trades.
newsitem.headline: Firm settles with CFTC, SEC over derivatives trades.

text.p: First Capital Strategists, a York, Penn., investment firm, agreed to pay $2.6 million to settle charges related to the loss of $137.6 million by a group of college endowment funds, federal regulators said Wednesday.
First Capital, which had been accused of failing to supervise trades that were associated with the investment loss, neither admitted nor denied any wrongdoing in the case.
The firm also agreed to leave the securities and futures business.
The $2.6 million will be paid as restitution to the client, Greenwich, Conn.-based Common Fund, a multi-billion dollar manager of endowments for 1,400 colleges and universities.

Common Fund, one of First Capital's biggest clients, lost $137.6 million as a result of the unauthorized trades made between 1992 and June 1995 by former derivatives trader Kent Ahrens, an SEC official said.
Ahrens last year settled federal charges and pleaded guilty to related criminal charges.
"This case is important because it's not just a failure to supervise," said Cheryl Scarboro, the SEC attorney handling the case. There was a "complete absence" of supervision, she said.

"The partners informed Common Fund immediately when they discovered the losses," said Joe Goldstein, a Washington attorney representing First Capital. "Everyone involved regrets the losses Common Fund suffered," he said.
Since Common Fund's losses became apparent, First Capital began winding down its operations, Goldstein said.
Common Fund has also sued to recover its losses from the illegal trades.
